messages.author: 712207b40d408846
messages.subject: negative binomial in lavaan
parts:
Hi lavaan community,

Can lavaan fit negative binomial instead of regular regression? My outcome measure is highly (positively) skewed. Since FIML cannot be used for binary options (if dichotomized), I am trying to figure out if I can use highly skewed outcome measures as they are.

Here is my model:

p16a18c24 <- ' 
# direct effect
myOutcome ~ c*myPredictor
# mediator
myMediator1 ~ a1*myPredictor
myOutcome ~ b1*myMediator1
myMediator2 ~ a2*myPredictor
myOutcome ~ b2*myMediator2
myMediator3 ~ a3*myPredictor
myOutcome ~ b3*myMediator3
# variances: any variable that was listed as DV
myOutcome ~~ myOutcome 
myMediator1 ~~ myMediator1
myMediator2 ~~ myMediator2
myMediator3 ~~ myMediator3
# covariances: mediators who are (positively) correlated with each other 
myMediator1 ~~ myMediator2
myMediator2 ~~ myMediator3
myMediator3 ~~ myMediator1
# intercepts: *1, only for DVs 
myOutcome ~ 1 
myMediator1 ~ 1
myMediator2 ~ 1
myMediator3 ~ 1
# indirect effects (a*b)
ab1 := a1*b1
ab2 := a2*b2
ab3 := a3*b3
# total effect
total := c + (a1*b1) + (a2*b2) + (a3*b3)
'
fit.p16a18c24 <- sem(p16a18c24,data=m,missing="fiml",se="bootstrap")
summary(fit.p16a18c24,fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE,rsquare=TRUE)

I would really appreciate your answer.

Thanks in advance,
NewInMediation

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: negative binomial in lavaan
parts: Can lavaan fit negative binomial instead of regular regression?

No, Mplus has appropriate link functions for counts, but lavaan only does for ordered factors.  If you specify your model using blavaan (Bayesian lavaan package, which also has a Google group forum to post questions), then it will write a JAGS script (the Bayesian software that actually fits the model), which you can adjust to add the appropriate link function and likelihood function for the data. 

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: negative binomial in lavaan
parts: I am wondering if there is an update on whether lavaan can fit negative binomial instead of regular regression.

No, and that is unlikely to change anytime in the near future (i.e., next few years).  The Bayesian option I alluded to in September handles missing data quite nicely, because JAGS automatically treats missing values as additional parameters to be estimated, with priors equivalent to the likelihoods specified for the corresponding observed data.  OpenMx also is quite flexible, so you could program it yourself, if you are capable:

http://openmx.ssri.psu.edu/thread/1433

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
